title: Odd parts preserve the noise representation
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\\rho\\in[-1,1]$, and let $\\varepsilon\\in[0,1]$. Suppose $g:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$ takes values in $[-1,1]$ and is the noise transform at correlation $\\rho$ of some function $f$ taking values in $[-1,1]$ whose stable influence at parameter $1-\\varepsilon$ is at most $\\varepsilon$ at every coordinate. Then the odd part $x\\mapsto(g(x)-g(-x))/2$ is also the noise transform at correlation $\\rho$ of a function taking values in $[-1,1]$ whose stable influence at parameter $1-\\varepsilon$ is at most $\\varepsilon$ at every coordinate.
hypotheses_covered: $g$ is a noise transform at correlation $\\rho$ of a bounded function with stable influences at most $\\varepsilon$ at parameter $1-\\varepsilon$
